title: Read Daniel's hand edit to Neighbour
tier_reason: reading his edit and writing down what it implies — nothing to walk back
ask: Daniel hand-edited Neighbour in the sprite editor. He left no note, which usually means routine cleanup rather than a decision about the look. The measurement: Neighbour: 53 pixels across 13 frames (walk down 1 · standing idle 1, walk down 2, walk down 4 · wave / action pose 1, walk up 2). The change shows up in: walk down, walk up, walk left, walk right, standing idle, wave / action pose. The silhouette moved, not just the interior shading. Look at it against the style guide draft and the rest of the sheet, and say in a few lines what his edit is telling you about the direction — whether it agrees with the guide, quietly contradicts it, or repeats something he has done before. If it is just tidying and there is nothing to learn, say exactly that in one line; a short honest answer beats manufactured significance. Do not propose amendments to the guide yet; he wants a look session before it is signed. This is evidence-gathering for that session.
first_action: Open assets/sprites/generated/neighbour.png and the ledger entry (step 1) in HQ, compare it with the style guide in docs/design/09-art-direction.md, and write down what the edit says about his taste.

result:
Opened both sheets' ledgers and lined the edit up against the Farmer's.

**This is not a direction. It is the Farmer's fix, repeated on the Farmer's twin.**

`neighbour.png` is `characters.png` with a palette remap — same walk cycle, pixel for pixel (CREDITS.md). On 3 September he hand-edited the Farmer twice and told us what he was doing: *"Some squares were white when they should be transparent. This occluded the background behind the character."*

His Neighbour edit is that second Farmer sweep, frame for frame:

| | Farmer, step 2 | Neighbour, last night |
|---|---|---|
| Frames touched | 0,1,3,**4**,5,6,7,8,9,11,12,13,14,15 | the same, minus frame 4 |
| Pixels | 56 | 53 |
| Added / recoloured | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Colours gained or lost | none | none |

Same bounding boxes too — frame 0 at (22,40) 2×5, frame 3 at (22,39) 5×6, and so on down the sheet. Every pixel erased, clustered at the feet, roughly eight wide and six tall at the base of the figure. He left no note because he had already written it twice.

Three things worth saying:

**"The silhouette moved" is a false alarm.** The measurement flags any erasure as a silhouette change. Nothing about the drawn child changed — he cleared the opaque white halo standing between her feet and the ground.

**It tells us nothing about the look, and something uncomfortable about the pipeline.** Of his seven real hand edits, five are this exact defect: Farmer twice, Chicken, Tomato, the fence set twice. He is the studio's alpha-cleanup pass, done by hand, one sheet at a time, thirteen days after the twin sheet got the same treatment.

**Three pixels are unaccounted for.** The Farmer got 56, the Neighbour 53 — frame 4 untouched and one pixel short in frame 14. Either the remap already caught them or he missed them. If he missed them, the halo is still there.

Against the guide: it has nothing to say here. It names ramps, coloured outlines, the contrast rule and the reserved overlay hues — not one line about what happens at a sprite's edge. I'm not proposing an amendment; that waits for the look session, as he asked. But this is the one item I'd carry into that session that came from measurement rather than taste.

**What accepting this starts:** a read-only sweep of every generated sheet for opaque white that should be transparent, a fix in the post-processing so it stops happening, and this question added to the look session agenda. Nothing touches a shipped sheet until he's seen the list.

Report per sheet: file, frame index, pixel count, coordinates. Include neighbour.png frames 4 and 14 specifically — the hand edit left 53 pixels where the identical Farmer sweep took 56, and the 3-pixel gap is frame 4 (2px) plus one pixel of frame 14.
follow_ups.why: Five of Daniel's seven hand edits are the same defect on different sheets, so the ones he has not opened yet almost certainly carry it too.

follow_ups.title: Make the sprite post-processing step erase leftover white edges automatically
follow_ups.first_action: In the Retro Diffusion post-processing path, add a step that converts edge-connected near-white opaque pixels to alpha 0 before a sheet is written, and a check that fails if a sheet lands with any. Do not re-run it over shipped sheets yet — that is a separate decision.
follow_ups.why: Daniel has now spent six sprite-editor sessions hand-erasing pixels a script can remove at generation time.

follow_ups.first_action: Add a line to docs/design/09-art-direction.md under the hand-edits section noting that the guide specifies ramps, coloured outlines, contrast and reserved hues but says nothing about alpha at a sprite's edge, and that this is a question for the look session rather than an amendment.
follow_ups.why: The gap is real and measured, and it should be in front of him when he signs the guide rather than found again afterwards.

recommend.question: Do we clean the white edges out of the art pipeline now, or leave it until the reskin replaces these sheets anyway?
recommend.answer: Fix it in the pipeline now, and hold the re-run over existing sheets until you have seen the list of what is affected.
recommend.why: You have personally hand-erased this same defect on six sheets over two weeks — it is a manual step that should not exist, and it will keep reappearing on every new sheet between now and the reskin.
recommend.instead: Leave it: every placeholder sheet gets replaced at the reskin, so you could accept a handful more hand edits and spend nothing on the pipeline until the new art lands.
